headline: All majors below the 200-day line in a fearful market; whales moving Bitcoin off exchanges while shorts liquidate and funding stays positive.
paragraphs: The regime is underwater across the board. Bitcoin sits at 64,610, down 48.2 percent from its 12-month high of 124,739, and trades below its 200-day simple moving average with no golden cross in sight. Ethereum mirrors the structure: 1,908 against a 4,817 peak (down 60.4 percent), below the 200-day, no uptrend signal. Solana is the weakest of the majors, down 70.1 percent from 247.6 to 73.99, and the smaller caps are no exception. XRP down 68 percent, BNB down 54.6 percent, ADA down 80.1 percent. Not one asset is trading above its 200-day line, and none show a golden cross. The broader market cap stands at 2.29 trillion (up 0.74 percent on the day), Bitcoin dominance at 56.6 percent. This is a secular downtrend measured in dollars and time.

Momentum is weak and fragmented. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 53.2, right at neutral, with MACD below signal line, telling you the prevailing downtrend has no acceleration behind it. Ethereum at RSI 55.8, also neutral, also below signal. Solana at RSI 47.0 (below 50, slightly soft), below signal. The interesting spots are BNB (RSI 59.3, MACD above signal, suggesting some internal lift despite the price position below the 200-day), ADA (RSI 65.5, above 60, in overbought territory on the 14-period, but still massively far from its high and still below the long-term line), and DOGE (RSI 42.1, MACD above signal, a divergence between weak momentum and uptrend signal). On the face of it, these small pockets of momentum divergence in a downtrend environment usually mean local rest or retest, not regime change.

Funding is positive and moderately expensive across Bitcoin and Ethereum, signaling that longs are paying to hold their positions. Bitcoin funding sits at 0.68 basis points per 8 hours (7.5 percent annualized), Ethereum at 0.72 basis points (7.9 percent annualized). That is not a panic funding flip, but it is not cheap either. Open interest is substantial: Bitcoin at 2.01 billion USD, Ethereum at 1.29 billion USD. The long-to-short ratio tells the story of positioning: Bitcoin at 1.27 (more longs, but not extreme), Ethereum at 1.69 (notably more bullish), Solana at 2.57 (highly bullish), and DOGE at 5.03 (extremely lopsided to the long side). Liquidations over the past 24 hours paint a directional picture: in Bitcoin, shorts are being cleared out (6.88 million USD in short liquidations versus 1.21 million in longs), and the same pattern holds in Ethereum (11.09 million in shorts versus 4.08 million in longs) and SOL (255 thousand in shorts versus 104 thousand in longs). XRP shows the opposite, with long liquidations (770 thousand) dwarfing short liquidations (15 thousand), a sign that the crowd on that asset is stretched in one direction. The market is not crowded, but the long side has room to unwind.

Whale flows and stablecoin positioning reveal a divergence between big money and crowd moves. Over the past 24 hours, Bitcoin has seen 115.6 million USD net move off exchanges (69.3 million inflow, 184.9 million outflow), suggesting that holders are consolidating into self-custody. This is a single-day print and should be weighted as such, but the four-week whale flow trend is instructive: minus 147.9 million, minus 86.6 million, then plus 1.08 billion, then plus 1.12 billion. The last two weeks show strong net buying and consolidation off exchange, a structural bid from large holders. Stablecoins total 305.8 billion USD, down 1.17 percent over 30 days, which means dry powder is contracting slightly. The biggest single move in the past day was 499.7 million USD in USDT moving from Binance to self-custody (off exchange), and a like amount moving onto Binance, a wash, but the cumulative effect is that large stablecoin reserves are cycling through exchange infrastructure, keeping it available for entry if conviction strikes. On the ETF front, Bitcoin saw a 1.3 million USD net outflow on August 5 (one day) but has taken in 348 million USD net over the last five sessions, same_direction_days of only 1 (meaning the flows are mixed). Ethereum has seen 1.4 million USD net inflow today and 64.4 million USD over five sessions, with same_direction_days of 2, a steadier bid.

The crowd is afraid, with the Fear and Greed index at 27 (in the 20 to 33 range for the month), and that fear is showing up in price structure: all majors well below long-term highs, all below 200-day lines, neutral to soft momentum. But the liquidation profile suggests longs are being flushed out selectively (especially in XRP), shorts are being cleared in Bitcoin and Ethereum, and big holders are consolidating coins off exchange while stablecoin levels remain substantial. This is the classic setup where sentiment and positioning diverge: the crowd is fearful and the longer-term trend is weak, but the margin structure is not screaming distress and the whale bid is present.

Watch for a sustained move in funding direction (a flip to negative would suggest shorts are paying more, a reversal in positioning), a return of any of the majors above the 200-day line (the regime line), and the direction of the whale flows over the next five trading sessions (consolidation off exchange persisting would confirm the structural bid, while a return to net exchange inflows would signal distribution into the rally). The tape is not broken, but it is not generating conviction either.
